Want to know the crazy thing with old racing cars? You steer with the wheel, throttle, and brake.

All 3. It makes sense once you get it, but until then it's maddening.

If you enter the corner too fast and brake late, the vehicle becomes unstable.

If you enter slowly and accelerate out, the vehicle becomes unstable.

If you enter at the optimal speed, you likely experience considerable understeer.

Thus, your only options are one of the first two, using the accelerator and/or brake to manage your turn. Frequently, you find yourself utilizing all three.

I was flying a flight simulator aircraft from somewhere in the eastern time zone, south to north. Just cruising along in the upper 300 flight levels, when all of a sudden both engines go out. Don't panic, did I just mess up my fuel conversions? Nope, I have good fuel. Did I bork up my checklist and forget something? Nope, engines are configured as they should be. I literally have no idea why both engines shut down at exactly the same time. I configure it to glide, get the auxiliary power unit turned on (it starts, good sign). Still don't panic, work towards air starting the engines. Still don't panic, engine one starts and goes, engine two starts and goes. Don't panic, just flew over a state border, and I know up ahead is an airport, so I can put it down very safely there. Still not panicking, pull up the charts for approach and accept a vectored arrival for emergency.

Praying the whole time, I nail the approach on the dots. Engines didn't shut down again. I sat there for an hour going over my procedures, trying to figure out what went wrong. I could never figure it out, except a bug in the aircraft.

Needless to say, always keep a level head. From up in the 300's down to the ground, I always had a couple plans in case the engines went out. The APU was still running just in case it was needed, but even as far down as the final 500 feet I was visually scanning for fields for a non-field landing.

edit - Actually, another person reminded me of another bad one I had. Final to a major airport one day, the weather in the area had been bad, but had improved by the time I landed. Unfortunately, I was using default weather and apparently one of the stations didn't get the memo. I was about 1000 feet up when the 15 knot headwind turned into a 20 knot tailwind, and I plummeted 900 feet towards the houses under the approach path.

Only 900 feet, because I was somehow able to halt the stall just above treetop level. Needless to say I just pushed the throttles to full and went around. My hands didn't stop shaking for another hour or so, and I had trouble sleeping that night due to the adrenaline.
Hence my flair, the first thing I decided to experiment with on the aircraft.

I met a woman three months ago. We were the results of a conspiracy of matchmakers who realized we both shared the same alma mater, a well-known university in the Midwest. She's 31, and an actress. Her most famous role had been about 5 years prior when she played one of about a dozen patients to die in a disaster on a medical drama. Most of her roles had been independent films, or glorified extras in poorly performing studio films. What made me fall in love almost instantly was her honesty. She actually saw me play my senior year. She even confessed to heckling me while drunk. I remember the game against our in-state rival; no goals, two terrible turnovers, and getting my ass kicked in a fight as the final horn sounded on a 6-0 drubbing. She was willing to give me shit about that game, and damn if I didn't love her for that.

We had been dating for three months when she invited me to go with her to her movie premiere. It was an independent drama about a woman trying to escape a cult, and she was one of the fellow cult members of the main female star. The best thing you could do in multiplayer to start is to find a server that has a decent mission and low population. Fly around, get some situational awareness, hell even go up with just heat-seeking missiles and electronic countermeasure pods. Draw the surface-to-air missile sites out of hiding. Learn to avoid and defend against launches, because if you’re going to hunt SAMs, you’re going to get shot at. Once you’re comfortable getting shot at, load up the suppression of enemy air defenses pod and a couple of bombs, and learn to do the close-in killing. Anti-aircraft systems are best left to cluster bombs or guided missiles, or even a two-person team to draw it out if hiding. Once you get the shorter range anti-radiation missiles, the more advanced ones are a piece of cake. Start small, get bigger. Do it in steps, and only move on once you’re comfortable. I’m at the point now that I know what’s firing on me by instinct (they’re doing what I’d do if I were them!), and I don’t usually get too concerned unless I’m at max weight.

I worked at a store that sold discounted items for various reasons, and it was large with a wide selection. Our day typically followed a routine of unusual customers coming in. For instance, from 9am to 11am was the time for older customers, where I had to explain to an elderly person that company policy prevented both negotiating prices and giving a 90% discount for a barely noticeable scuff on an item. It was often a parade of eccentric individuals, made more interesting by the town being the hub of a rural county. Little did we know, the oddness was within us all along.

I was restocking the front area with candy (now with extra surprises!), and the only other male coworker was up front discussing the significance of a 3-liter bottle of soda when a new coworker approached us.

As a side note, one of our supervisors was a very devout individual. She embodied all the aspects of her faith but often avoided the moral responsibilities that came with it, using her beliefs as a shield when confronted about her behavior. She was quite large and would often drop items, expecting the male staff to pick them up for her. Additionally, one of her (highly inappropriate) interview questions was about the church affiliation of the candidates. This is relevant because...

The new employee approached us. She appeared to be in her mid-40s, with a rural demeanor, short and somewhat stocky. I had seen her lift multiple heavy items the day before, so I knew she was not someone I wanted to engage with. My coworker was discussing the peculiar 3-liter bottle of questionable soda as an affront to a higher power when she chimed in;

“I believe there is only one true God, and Jesus is his son. There is no other religion, Islam is a religion of immoral people, and the Jews were responsible for Jesus' death.”

This abruptly ended the conversation. However, she continued. Over the next concerning 10 minutes without any customers, the discussion veered into:

Immigration! “People from certain countries are not truly religious. They should have to convert to our faith to enter our country.”

Numerology! “The population of a certain country is 666 million people at this very moment. Did you know they restrict their population growth? They are inviting trouble!”

Sociology! “People of different ethnic backgrounds might be decent, but their circumstances were changed by a higher power because they lost faith.”

Economics! “I have been provided for, and I am here because of my belief.”

(Seriously, our custodian had to clean up a mess in the restroom recently because some individuals left it in a terrible state, and we can’t ban them because they attend the same church as the aforementioned supervisor. This is not an ideal workplace.)

Ecology! “Everything on this earth is for my use, and I will drive my car as much as I want because that honors Him.”

She gradually wound down, and fortunately for me, she finished her little sermon just in time for me to explain to an elderly lady that 90 cents wouldn’t cover a $10 purchase. The eccentric lady returned to her impressive lifting in the stock room when my coworker remarked;

“Ah...thank goodness she feels the heat for her beliefs!”

And I ended up snorting in front of the little old lady.

The first amendment isn’t just about you speaking freely. It’s about people with extreme ideas being allowed to advertise their positions, so civil society can mock and ignore.

Unfortunately, it’s become socially acceptable to allow individuals with prejudiced views a lot of leeway under the guise of free speech. The truth is that they’re allowed to talk, but nobody is forced to give them a platform, and whoever wants to is free to mock them for their foolish, foolish ideas.

1) Have your child tell the bully to stop, and to inform you when they have done so.

2) Have your child report the incident to the teacher, and ensure you have the date of this occurrence.

3) Send a note to the teacher indicating that this behavior is still happening.

4) Contact school administration, and document your communication.

5) Teach your child about self-defense.

Violence doesn’t resolve every issue. There are instances where what occurs may be a misunderstanding, something your child is involved in, or even an event that did not transpire as described. A couple of incidents do not constitute a pattern, and often you can find a way to resolve the situation. However, some individuals may only respond to physical confrontation, which they will remember. I only have daughters, so I understand that the physical aspect may not be as prominent in bullying. Nevertheless, I will assure my daughters that they have my full support when it comes to standing up for themselves or others.

By documenting everything that happens, when your child defends themselves and the school fails to acknowledge the issue and blames your child, you will have a clear record of the school’s failure to protect your child. Avoid starting with threats of legal action or media involvement. Begin with a meeting to discuss how the situation was handled, and gradually increase the pressure in a calm and reasonable manner.

When I was younger, my parent made it clear that any trouble at school was unacceptable, and I would face serious consequences for any issues. Once, a peer grabbed my hair and threw me down during recess, and I was punished at home. I spent many years being bullied because I chose to ignore it. Ignoring it is not an option; the only way to address the problem is to escalate the situation gradually, until the last resort becomes necessary.

When I was 12 or 13, my parents drove me to the nearest video rental store to rent a game for a classic gaming console. What followed is one of my greatest misses, in a way.

Now, there were three people who worked at this video store; the owner, who was probably in his 20s-30s and was a gamer even back in the early-mid 90s when this happened. The second was a heavyset man with a goatee, resembling a character from a popular animated film. The third, however, was a younger woman, probably in the 18-26 age range.

She was at the desk that day, and she and I were the only people in the store. Nothing was amiss, no weirdness going on in the store. I went back to the game section and started searching for whatever game I wanted to rent that night. After about 15 minutes, I picked the game, got my money out, and went to the front desk where, to my shock, the woman was not wearing a shirt. She had stripped down to her bra.

Okay, I'll power through this. I'm not sure what she was doing, because it was the middle of the summer, and it was probably 90 degrees out that day. She's probably just hot, yeah, that's it.

Then she asks the question that I still wonder what she was trying to do.

"Have you ever seen a grown woman like me?"

Uhhh

I paid and left. Looking back on the situation, the whole thing was really strange.

Right around that time, coincidentally, I started paying more attention to the girls at my school.

Also, I never saw the woman again. I tried to slyly bring it up with the owner later on, and he gave me the look of a guy who knew why I was asking. He changed the subject to the games I was renting.

When I mentioned the next school year that I almost scored with someone possibly twice my age, nobody believed me.

It was during a recreational hockey game. The player was acting aggressively and knocked down one of my teammates with a hit that would have been a penalty even in a league that allowed checking. I was fed up with his behavior and stood up for my teammate by taking him down after the whistle. He got back up and charged into the fray, yelling about wanting to fight me and/or some kind of pastry. He was shouting a lot of things I couldn’t hear. I’m not a quick thinker, but I knew that I didn’t want to fight, get suspended for the season, and lose $200 for my troubles. So I yelled back “screw you, I’m a pacifist!” I blame watching a certain cult classic film a lot at the time.

The comment completely confused him. He calmed down immediately because he couldn’t process what just happened. A couple of his teammates laughed when I said it. One of them asked me why I said it after the game, and I just said that I didn’t want to lose $200.
